key_features.classic_presentation: IBS presents with CHRONIC RECURRENT crampy abdominal pain (at least once per week for 3+ months) associated with CHANGE IN BOWEL HABITS (diarrhea, constipation, or alternating). Pain is CRAMPY, INTERMITTENT, 3-6/10 severity, RELIEVED by defecation. Location: Lower abdomen, diffuse, migrating. NO alarm features: NO blood in stool, NO weight loss, NO nocturnal symptoms, NO fever. Key associated symptoms: BLOATING and gas, mucus in stool (without blood), sense of incomplete evacuation. Symptoms WORSE with stress or certain foods. Pattern: Chronic over months to years, waxing and waning. Key positives: Pain better after bowel movement, symptoms for >6 months, triggered by stress/food. Key negatives: NEW onset in patient >50 years requires workup to rule out cancer. Blood in stool rules out IBS. Weight loss, fever, or nocturnal diarrhea suggests organic disease not IBS.

red_flags: Blood in stool - needs colonoscopy to rule out IBD or colon cancer
Unintentional weight loss - organic pathology, not IBS
New onset after age 50 - higher risk of colon cancer, needs colonoscopy
Nocturnal symptoms waking patient from sleep - suggests organic disease
